newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metalworkers near deal in last major region.
newsitem.headline: German metalworkers near deal in last major region.

text.p: German metal and engineering workers in the southern region of Nordwuerttemberg were due to begin talks on Tuesday confident that they would be able to force employers into a climb-down on planned labour cost cuts.
Nordwuerttemberg, with some 600,000 employed in the sector, is the last big engineering region where accords guaranteeing workers continued sick pay at full salary have not been signed.

A federal law introduced in October allowed employers to reduce sick pay to 80 percent of salary, but mass protests and the threat of strikes in the industry have dissuaded the vast majority of employers from implementing the cuts.

Following a break-through deal signed in the northern state of Lower Saxony two weeks ago, contracts securing full sick pay have now been signed for some two-thirds of the 3.2 million workers in the west German metal and engineering sectors.
"The employers here cannot assume that they will be able to change anything significant (from the Lower Saxony agreement)," a spokeswoman for the IG Metall trade union said in Stuttgart.

The Lower Saxony agreement, which has been adopted by regions including the steel-producing state of North Rhine-Westphalia and the large Bavarian engineering region, includes a 1.5 pay rise next year and 2.5 percent in 1998.

Nordwuerttemberg's federation of regional metal employers, the VMI, said going into the talks that it accepted that the Lower Saxony deal had set a model for other agreements but that it wanted any agreement it reached to reflect "regional characteristics" in Nordwuerttemberg.
Some 180,000 engineering workers in the northern German coastal region have still to reach a wage deal with employers.
